sourceInformation.genre: Racing (arcade time attack), with track-building puzzles
sourceInformation.perspective: Third-person chase camera; orbiting camera on the title, attract and editor screens
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge 2D engine and 3D engine v0.85.2 (commit 4390a98), three.js r182 (WebGL 2 fallback), Rapier 0.19.3, esbuild 0.25.12, playwright-core 1.63.0 (checks)
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's toon 3D style with ink outlines and pixel-art UI, all drawn by code (pen parts, no image files)
sourceInformation.animation: Code-driven car, checkpoint gate and camera motion; no rig animation
sourceInformation.audio: Engine songs and effects; car engine and babble voices synthesised in code
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, ghost mode (client 1.4.0)
sourceInformation.testing: 24 headless checks behind one command: roads, car physics, bot on all 15 roads, run rules, scene flow, a scripted whole-game playthrough, online ghost session, editor and puzzles; Playwright boot and screenshot checks of the built file
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown

testingFeedback: About eight real bugs were caught; three were critical: the steering sign (no bot finished), the countdown braking the car off the line, and loops drawn face-down so the car drove through them.
Three of them were game-breaking: no run could be driven, every run began with a respawn, and loops could not be driven at all.
The most helpful test was a bot run of every road that counts respawns, because it exposed the three critical bugs at once.
The least helpful test was the page's no-error check: it passed while the game was broken, and a silent canvas stub hid the look until screenshots were taken.
engineFeedback: The pen for code-drawn parts, the fixed camera, and the engine's menus, pause and settings were the best parts of the engine.
Stuck on the 3D track and vehicle: they don't drive a loop, and the boot runs asynchronously, so tests must await game.booted.
The road mesh and colliders, the car model, the bot, the run rules and every mode are my own; the engine supplied only the world, camera, menus and boot.
The hardest part was the 3D side's size and the headless canvas, which needed a stub before the world would build under Node.
Changed in the engine: E1 pen frame (any orientation), E2 camera up vector, E4 analog triggers, E5 PlayStation glyphs by default, E6 exported toon bands, each for a reason in the plan.
I would add one call that builds a racing road with a loop, or a documented road-mesh helper, since that is what this game needed most.
promptFeedback: The plan's detail on the car model, the controls and the validated physics appendix was the most useful part of the prompt.
The plan is sized for a far bigger build than one session; the title rule, where TASK.md wins, was clear.
The hardest thing was scope: a loop road and a split screen are each still bigger than this session.
I would add a smaller first milestone and a note on what to cut first when time runs short.

aiHub.name: CRACKMANIA
aiHub.description: A desert time-attack racer: fifteen roads in three environments, medals, ghosts, a survival gauntlet, hot-seat cups, a track editor and puzzles, and AI Hub ghost races.
aiHub.controls: R2/W gas, L2/S brake, left stick or arrows steer, Circle/Enter respawn, Triangle/R restart
